data.narrative:
NordSpace, a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Rahul Goel, has raised $38M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 13 total peers: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage progression against the $38M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $76M. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient same- or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum dataset thresholds (0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage identified across the narrow Space & Aerospace universe). Public-comp anchoring via EV/Revenue multiple could not proceed; while the sector median P/S stands at 23.9x across the 5 public tickers, NordSpace's revenue is not on file, precluding multiple application.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $65M to $87M, with a median point of $76M. This narrow range reflects heavy reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-stage disclosure (limiting public multiple applicability) and sparse private-peer comparables at the Series A stage in space technology. Validation through customer concentration, burn rate, and capital efficiency metrics would strengthen conviction in this estimate.
